name: Machiavelli
description: Machiavelli is a sophisticated Italian card game of the Rummy family, named after the political philosopher NiccolÃ² Machiavelli for its tactical complexity and the ability to 'manipulate' the board. Unlike standard Rummy where melds are static once played, players in Machiavelli can dismantle, rearrange, and recombine any cards already on the table to help them play cards from their hand. It is practically identical to the game Rummikub but played with standard cards.

history.origins: Developed in post-WWII Italy as a variation of 'Manipulation Rummy'. Its rules were popularized in Mediterranean card clubs during the 1960s.
timeline: 1950s: Rules for 'Rummy a Terre' involve basic manipulation.
1970s: The name 'Machiavelli' becomes standard in Italian gaming circles.
1980s: The game's mechanics are used as the basis for the global hit board game Rummikub.
Present: One of the most common family card games in Italy and widely played on digital platforms.
history.cultural: Seen as a 'smart' game, played in cafes and university lounges.
history.evolution: The game was traditionally played with Jokers, but modern tournament rules often omit them to increase the challenge of forming natural sequences.

setup.dealing: Each player receives 13 cards (variants range from 11 to 15).
setup.equipment: Two standard decks, playing surface for melds.

rules.objective: Be the first to play all cards from your hand onto the table.
rules.gameplay: On your turn, you must either: 1. Play at least one card from your hand into a valid meld (new or existing). 2. Draw one card from the stock and end your turn.
keyRules: Must play at least one new card from hand each turn you play
All table cards must form valid melds at end of turn
Can manipulate any existing melds on the table
Draw one card if unable or unwilling to play

strategy.basic: Don't 'dump' your easiest cards early. If you see a way to play a 7 of Hearts, wait until you have another card that depends on it. The more cards you put on the table, the more options your OPPONENTS have on their turns.
strategy.intermediate: The Big Reveal: Wait until you can play 4-5 cards at once by rearranging the whole board. This 'explodes' your hand and often ends the game before opponents can react to the new board state.
strategy.advanced: Defensive Manipulation: If you see an opponent looking for a 5 of Spades to finish their sequence, and that 5 is already in a 'Set of 5s' on the table, try to move that 5 into a DIFFERENT sequence that is harder for them to access.
tips: Sequences are better for manipulation than Sets. A sequence of 3-4-5-6 can be split into two 3-card melds if you have the right cards; a 3-card Set is 'atomic' and cannot be split.
Always scan for 'orphan' cards. If you see a sequence of 4 cards, you can potentially take one end and use it elsewhere.

scoring.description: After a player goes out, remaining players count points in their hands. Face cards = 10, Ace = 1 or 11, number cards = face value.
scoring.winCondition: First player to play all cards from their hand wins the round.

synthesis.shortDescription: An Italian Rummy variant where players can manipulate any melds on the table to play cards from their hand.
